- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., -0.4 → +0.3), model delays correction — forecast should adjust downward 2–3 days before sentiment turns positive.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > +15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven corrections — add 2–3% buffer if sentiment volatility > 0.3 std dev.
- If sentiment is flat (avg ±0.1) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days if trend persists.
